answer: The marble cipher sonnet: a claimant carves a fourteen-line sonnet into a marble tablet, each line encoded with a cipher key, and sets it into a named public wall. Two cipher wardens decode the sonnet against the registered key in four days, checking depth against the marble register and the quarry mark on its back. A wrong key, copied sonnet, or mismatched mark voids the claim, burns a 220-credit stake, and bars the workshop two seasons. Forging 1,000 identities means carving 1,000 tablets and writing 1,000 sonnets by hand, while one honest carver finishes one tablet before dusk.
